news.title: Let’s give Robin a break
news.description: SEN. Robinhood “Robin” Padilla is, by far, one of the most colorful, recognized and polarizing lawmakers in the country today. Known for his onscreen “bad boy” roles during the turbulent early 1990s, Robin had also been one offscreen: he once got into a fistfight at Baguio’s popular Spirits Disco, which I witnessed. As a movie icon, Robin was known to be ill-tempered, as well as a venerable Don Juan and a man whose trademark garbled speech was like that of a drunken sailor. His offscreen notoriety abruptly ended in 1992, when he was arrested after sideswiping a balut vendor in Angeles City, Pampanga, and police discovered several high-powered firearms in his Pajero.

news.title: JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley restrict third-party AI agents amid banking security concerns
news.description: Major US lenders are restricting access to customer accounts for third-party AI agents as concerns grow over automated systems acting beyond users’ instructions. JPMorgan Chase and Charles Schwab have warned of the risks, while Morgan Stanley has blocked external agents from its platforms, despite reporting no known rogue-agent incidents.

news.title: US banks are blocking third-party AI agents access to customer accounts, sources say
news.description: Major US banks, including Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan Chase, are blocking third-party AI agents from transactions. This decision comes after concerns that AI agents might act independently without customer instructions. Both Morgan Stanley and Charles Schwab have reported blocking unauthorized agent access to their platforms. Banking executives are increasingly worried about the risks associated with AI technology in financial transactions.

news.title: US SEC proposes wider retail investor access to private assets amid risk concerns
news.description: The SEC has proposed new rules to expand access to private assets typically available only to wealthy investors. These rules aim to allow more professionals to qualify as accredited investors, which may lead to higher returns. Critics express concern that this move could expose retail investors to significant risks and fees. Additionally, proposed changes would allow closed-end funds to redeem shares more frequently and offer varied share classes.

news.title: SingSaver, Singapore's Leading Personal Finance Platform, Launches Home Loans Segment
news.description: Affiliate partnership with Redbrick Mortgage Advisory gives SingSaver users bank-by-bank rate comparison and advice through to applicationThe launch takes SingSaver into Singapore's largest household debt category, worth S$296.4 billion, where the gap between bank home loan rates and the HDB concessionary rate of 2.6% can add up to hundreds of dollars a month for borrowers SINGAPORE, Sept. 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SingSaver, Singapore's leading personal finance comparison platform and part of Nasdaq-listed MoneyHero Group (NASDAQ: MNY), today launched a Home Loans comparison category in partnership with Redbrick Mortgage Advisory. The launch takes SingSaver into the largest category of household debt in Singapore and extends its product suite beyond credit cards, personal loans, insurance and brokerage.
